checks.name: date_of_birth is within a plausible range
checks.definition:
checks for birth_registrations:
  - failed rows:
      fail query: |
        SELECT registration_number, date_of_birth
        FROM birth_registrations
        WHERE date_of_birth < DATE '1900-01-01' OR date_of_birth > CURRENT_DATE
      name: date_of_birth is within a plausible range
      # Explicit high ceiling, not reliance on Soda's own (documented,
      # unfixed) bug that "failed rows" checks ignore samples limit
      # entirely (GitHub sodadata/soda-core#1985 - see plans/qa-
      # pipeline.md #29). Today this check's own true failing-row count
      # never comes close to it on this fixture; the point is that this
      # project's *intent* - "get every failing row this check finds" -
      # is now stated explicitly, so a future Soda release that starts
      # enforcing samples limit properly doesn't silently reintroduce a
      # 100-row cap here without anyone having decided that's acceptable.
      samples limit: 100000
      attributes:
        check_id: 
          data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.date_of_birth.range_check_soda
        introduced_date: "2026-09-13"
        description: "Date of birth must be a plausible real date, not in the future
          or absurdly old."
        changelog: []

resourceAttributes.name: check_id
resourceAttributes.value: data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.date_of_birth.range_check_soda

resourceAttributes.name: description

checks.name: multiple birth records have a matching sibling
checks.definition:
checks for birth_registrations:
  - failed rows:
      fail query: |
        SELECT a.registration_number
        FROM birth_registrations a
        WHERE a.is_multiple_birth = true
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM birth_registrations b
            WHERE b.is_multiple_birth = true
              AND b.registration_number != a.registration_number
              AND b.date_of_birth = a.date_of_birth
              AND b.place_of_birth_facility IS NOT DISTINCT FROM a.place_of_birth_facility
              AND b.registering_parent_1_name IS NOT DISTINCT FROM a.registering_parent_1_name
          )
      name: multiple birth records have a matching sibling
      samples limit: 100000
      attributes:
        check_id: 
          data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.is_multiple_birth.sibling_match_soda
        introduced_date: "2026-01-15"
        description: "Every record flagged as a multiple birth should have a matching
          sibling row for the same birth event."
        changelog: []

resourceAttributes.value: data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.is_multiple_birth.sibling_match_soda

checks.name: recent birth dates present (freshness)
checks.definition:
checks for birth_registrations:
  - failed rows:
      fail query: |
        SELECT 1 WHERE NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM birth_registrations WHERE date_of_birth >= date_registered - INTERVAL '7' DAY
        )
      name: recent birth dates present (freshness)
      attributes:
        check_id: 
          data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.date_of_birth.freshness_soda
        introduced_date: "2026-01-15"
        description: "At least one birth registration should have a date_of_birth
          within 7 days of this run's own date_registered."
        changelog:
          - date: "2026-09-17T00:00:00Z"
            description: "Anchored to this run's own date_registered instead of real
              wall-clock CURRENT_DATE, which is why this check was permanently red.
              Paired with a new inject_stale_delivery generator defect so the check
              has something genuine to catch."
            author: "Keith Moss"
            breaking: true

# --- "Proportion of records since a certain date" ---------------------------
# Scopes the same invalid-value check to only the last 24 hours of extracts,
# so a brand-new drift is caught fast rather than being diluted by months of
# clean historical data sitting in the same table. This is what turns "check
# the whole table" into "check what we've received lately" - not a separate
# feature, just the same metric computed over a filtered subset.

resourceAttributes.value: data-asset-1.registry-services.birth-registrations.stg_birth_registrations.date_of_birth.freshness_soda

resourceAttributes.name: description
resourceAttributes.value: At least one birth registration should have a date_of_birth within 7 days of this run's own date_registered.

queries.name: 259.birth_registrations.birth_registrations.aggregation[0]
queries.sql:
SELECT 
  COUNT(*),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN date_registered < date_of_birth THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN extract_timestamp < date_registered OR extract_timestamp > date_registered + INTERVAL '1' DAY THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN date_of_birth IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN registration_number IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN child_given_names IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (child_given_names IS NULL) AND NOT (REGEXP_MATCHES(child_given_names, '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN child_family_name IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (child_family_name IS NULL) AND NOT (REGEXP_MATCHES(child_family_name, '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN place_of_birth_suburb IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (place_of_birth_suburb IS NULL) AND NOT (place_of_birth_suburb IN ('Fremantle','Subiaco','Joondalup','Rockingham','Mandurah','Midland','Armadale','Cannington','Morley','Cockburn Central','Scarborough','Victoria Park','Bunbury','Albany','Geraldton','Kalgoorlie','Broome','Karratha','Port Hedland','Busselton','Northam','Narrogin','Esperance','Collie','Mount Lawley','Leederville','Wembley','Innaloo','Success','Baldivis','Ellenbrook','Butler','Balga','Girrawheen','Maddington','Gosnells','Kwinana','Hamilton Hill','Beaconsfield','South Perth','Bentley','Willetton','Riverton','Karrinyup','Currambine','Clarkson','Yanchep','Byford','Waroona','Manjimup','Margaret River')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN date_registered IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN extract_timestamp IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN registering_parent_1_name IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (registering_parent_1_name IS NULL) AND NOT (REGEXP_MATCHES(registering_parent_1_name, '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN registering_parent_2_name IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (registering_parent_2_name IS NULL) AND NOT (REGEXP_MATCHES(registering_parent_2_name, '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z. -]*$')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (sex IS NULL) AND NOT (sex IN ('M','F','X')) THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN place_of_birth_facility IS NULL THEN 1 END),
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT (source_system_record_id IS NULL) AND NOT (REGEXP_MATCHES(source_system_record_id, '^SRC-[0-9]{9}$')) THEN 1 END) 
FROM birth_registrations
